deep.reconstruction:
This is page '4' of an early (1983) draft of what became the theory of derivators. Here H is a 2-functor A ↦ H(A) on small categories, with restriction functors f^*: H(B) → H(A) for f: A → B, admitting adjoints f_! ⊣ f^* ⊣ f_*. Hot_H denotes H(e), the value on the final category.

(1) Homotopy limit functor. With π_A: A → e the projection, Grothendieck defines ∏_A := (π_A)_*: H(A) → Hot_H, the homotopy limit (dual to the homotopy colimit ∫_A = (π_A)_!, which appears on the preceding pages of the draft).

(2) Transitivity. For f: A → B one has π_A = π_B∘f. Hence (π_A)_* ≅ (π_B)_* f_*, i.e. ∏_A X ≅ ∏_B f_*(X). This is the 'Fubini/transitivity' property of homotopy limits.

(3) Diagonal margin note, partly illegible. It apparently states that the existence of the f_*^H, together with a property of the f^* of commuting with products ('∏') in the H(A), is what is needed or implied. In other words, the right-derivator side requires f^* to preserve the relevant products.

(4) Duality. Put H°(A) = H(A)^op and f^*_{H°} = (f^*_H)^op. Passing to opposite categories turns left adjoints into right adjoints, so f_!^{H°} = (f_*^H)^op and f_*^{H°} = (f_!^H)^op. Consequently homotopy colimits ∫ and homotopy limits ∏ are exchanged.

(5) Additive case. If each H(A) is additive (e.g. k-linear over a fixed ring k) and the f^* are additive, then the adjoints f_!, f_* are additive. This holds because an adjoint of an additive functor between additive categories automatically preserves finite biproducts.

The page serves the axiomatic set-up of a 'homotopy theory' as a system of categories H(A) indexed by diagram shapes, with Kan extensions. It belongs to the line Pursuing Stacks (1983) → Les Dérivateurs (c. 1990–91).
errors: The naive dual H°(A) = H(A)^op is a subtle point. It reverses the variance on 2-cells and, more importantly, does not carry a derivator satisfying the base-change (comma-category) axiom to one of the same type. In the dual, f_! = (f_*)^op would be computed by the comma categories b\A instead of A/b. In the later Les Dérivateurs the dual is taken to be D°(A) = D(A^op)^op. The 1983 formula is fine for the formal adjoint-swapping and for the statement that ∫ and ∏ are exchanged, but it is not the correct dual in the full axiomatic sense.
The margin note is too fragmentary to check. As read, it asserts a link between the existence of f_* and f^* commuting with products, which is plausible but not stated precisely.

ideas.what: Homotopy limit as right adjoint ∏_A = (π_A)_* of the constant-diagram functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (derivators), Heller (homotopy theories, 1988), Franke; holim going back to Bousfield–Kan
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (c. 1990–91); Pursuing Stacks discusses the related setting

ideas.modern_name: composition of homotopy right Kan extensions / Fubini for holim

ideas.what: Dual system H°, exchanging f_! and f_*, and ∫ with ∏
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Les Dérivateurs (with the A^op correction); Heller
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs, ch. I (dual derivator D°(A) = D(A°)°)

ideas.what: Additive case: adjoints of additive restriction functors are additive
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard category theory; additive and triangulated derivators studied by Grothendieck, Maltsiniotis, Keller, Groth

missed.claim: This is an early (1983) form of the dual derivator using H(A)^op rather than H(A^op)^op. It documents the evolution of the definition between Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs, and is of historical interest only.
missed.quote: Posons H°(A) = H(A)°, on trouve des f^*_{H°} = (f^*_H)°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Dates Grothendieck's axiomatics of derivators, including the duality and additive cases, to 1983, and shows that the correct form of the dual was found only later.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine formal setup of homotopy limits, duality and additivity in a derivator-like framework, all later published in Les Dérivateurs. The only notable point is the early, naive form of the dual.
transcription_corrections: '∏_A = (π_A)_*' is written below ∏_A with an '=' sign (vertical '||'). It is a definition, not a separate line.
The formula reads '∏_A X = ∏_B f_*(X)': the struck-out symbol before it is a crossed-out ∏_A, and 'f_*' is written as 'f' with a subscript (likely *).
The diagonal margin note reads approximately: 'et l'existence des f_*^H / la propriété des f^* de commuter aux [produits?] des H(A) ...'. Its last lines are illegible.
'Hot_H' is written 'Hot' with subscript H, i.e. H(e).
